title: Area Worksheets: Counting Square Units
intro: Use unit squares to distinguish area from perimeter.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Cover a rectangle with equal squares without gaps or overlaps. Count the squares, then connect rows and columns to multiplication.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

3 rows of 4 squares cover 12 square units.

Count each square once, or add the rows: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

Ask your student

What does one square represent?

If your student needs help

If the student counts grid lines, shade one complete square and count the regions together.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set has six distinct rectangular grids with one to five rows and one to five columns. All tiles are whole squares. Count them or use equal rows; the answer key gives the total area. Use the working space to show a repeated sum or multiplication equation.
